740081402.text: Your wish is my command. Please, follow me. Our destination is not far from the Court of Fontaine...

740082601.text: Wow, it looks so heavy, and so hot and stuffy...

740082602.text: Actually, you can place Mist Flowers wrapped in cloth inside to lower the temperature! As for the weight, well, just put it underwater.

740082603.text: There's no time for delay! Let's go, my friends!

740080201.text: How will we open that door and proceed onward...

740080202.text: Ooh, so this is the "Forum" you were talking about! There are so many books everywhere — they must really have been dedicated to studying and conducting research...

740080203.text: Paimon would never have guessed that they were a secret society plotting to overthrow the government of Fontaine!

740080204.text: As the saying goes, dear Paimon, "Knowledge is power." This is especially true for the Liliacruces Forum.

740080205.text: You should understand that with great knowledge comes great power. And once great power is yours to command... There will only be one path left to you.

740080206.text: Uh... Paimon doesn't think that logic really holds water, but you're the local, not Paimon, so Paimon'll trust you know what you're talking about and leave it at that!

740080207.text: They seem to have been researching some amazing things, though. And we've already seen plenty of stuff that obviously isn't from here on the way...

740080401.text: According to my research, this should be the treasure vault of the Liliacruces Forum. The riches we seek should be within.

740080405.text: Paimon thought the vault would be full of glittering, golden Mora, as dazzling as the sun...

740080406.text: You should know, my dear friends, that just as the truly wealthy do not flaunt it in anything as shallow as appearances, real treasure...

740080407.text: Ohh, Paimon knows what you're about to say— "the real treasure was the friends we made along the way!"

740080408.text: Uh, I was about to say that the real treasure is not so easily revealed, but you're also exactly right, Paimon. I have to say, I could have never come up with something so wise and philosophical!

740080409.text: Regardless, the purpose of our expedition is to uncover the treasure the institute has hidden away for centuries. And I am convinced beyond a shadow of a doubt that the treasure is hidden in this room, so let's hurry up and get in there and find it!

740080410.text: Uh, are you sure? Paimon doesn't see anything in there besides a few broken ruin mechanisms...

740080411.text: Your words wound me, my friend. We're partners who are seeking the institute's long-lost treasure together. Do you really doubt me?

740080412.text: Okay, so is this a forum, or an institute?

740080413.text: #Ah, about that... Let's just say that different records refer to it differently! But my dear {NICKNAME}, the name isn't the important thing— we should keep our eyes on the prize!

740080414.text: What we are talking about isn't merely a matter of hundreds of thousands or even millions of Mora... but a vast secret trove of hundreds of millions of Mora, sleeping within the vault!

740080416.text: And there are other priceless items in the vault, too! Like, uh... There's the all-powerful Liliacruces Holy Sword, which can pierce through armor and destroy the soul itself! A magical item powerful beyond compare!

740080417.text: Wh—Whoa, Paimon had no idea! And it's all in this vault!?

740080418.text: Precisely! And if you ask me, every moment that we spend bantering here increases the risk of us being beaten to the treasure by all sorts of scrupleless ruffians who will stop at nothing to steal it!

740080419.text: We can't let that happen! It's our treasure...

740080420.text: #See, you get me! Then in that case, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, please go forth and recover the treasure. I'll make sure to watch the rear!

740080503.text: I'm so very sorry, I made a terrible mistake. It was only during our expedition that I realized this wasn't the former grounds of the Liliacruces Forum, but rather the ruins of the Institute of Natural Philosophy.

740080504.text: There's no treasure here, but there are lots of experiments on machinery and energy. And now, my dearest friends, another experiment is about to begin.

740080505.text: As for treasures, it would be wrong to say there aren't any at all here... As seasoned adventurers, I'm sure you've accumulated quite a bit of Mora and other precious items over the course of your journey?

740080506.text: I will return after the conclusion of the experiment to collect the "treasures" you are sure to leave behind. Ah, and don't you worry, my friends— I'll be sure to put them to good use.

740080507.text: Virgil! You... You lied to us!

740080510.text: So you knew, and still decided to step into my trap? You're the kind of person I despise the most. So arrogant and disdainful! You blasted fools all treat me like an idiot! Even a couple of foreign hillb—

740080511.text: ...Hmph, whatever. According to the records here, this machine is a "special" Ruin Grader. No matter how good you are, even if you can handle Ruin Guards, you're still only made of flesh and bone.

740080512.text: As to what makes it "special," I'll leave you to find out in your own good time. Goodbye, my dear "partners."

subQuests.subQuestName: Explore the former site of the Liliacruces Forum

740080801.text: Let me see... Hmph, so this is actually the "Institute of Natural Philosophy"? Looks like the wrong place after all...

740080802.text: Ho, so there were things like this hidden here, how fascinating... I can use it against Sonny and the others...

740080803.text: Should be able to make use of this laboratory... Take care of things first...

subQuests.subQuestName: Leave the water and talk to Virgil

740081301.text: Anyway, let's hope nothing like that will happen in the future!

740081302.text: The future? Who cares about that? I'll be dead long before then, so why should I worry about the people alive then? What do the people and Fontaine of the future have to do with me?

740081303.text: I would pay my respects to my family and friends. After all, they raised me, and have done many things for me. But have the people of the future done anything for you, for me? So what do we owe them? Isn't that right?

740081306.text: ...Ahem, that's what I might have said about the issue of flooding if I lacked both patriotism and a sense of civic responsibility! Pretty abominable!

740081307.text: Anyway, sorry for digressing. There should be a way to open the door below. Let's take a look around to see if there are any clues or keys.

740081308.text: I'll also try to see if I can find anything in the associated files, my dear friends.

subQuests.subQuestName: Find a way to open the path forward

740080701.text: Brilliant! Now we can continue further into the institute's depths. As expected of a seasoned adventurer!

740080702.text: Eh? Aren't we investigating the Forum? So is it a forum, or an institute?

740080704.text: And forgive me for asking this out of the blue, but did either of you ever run into anyone who was looking for me? Or did you tell anyone else about our encounter?

740080705.text: Eh? Hmm... Paimon doesn't think so!

740080706.text: What's wrong, Virgil? Do you owe someone a ton of Mora?

740080707.text: Hahaha, no, of course not... It just occurred to me that I should let you know that there are many greedy goons who are also after the Liliacruces Forum's secret treasure.

740080708.text: They're very different from us. They're willing to do anything to achieve their goals, so I've always refused to work with them. As I know the most about the treasure's whereabouts, they have me in their sights.

740080709.text: I've spent a long time hiding from their prying eyes and looking for partners I can trust. It is my luck to have finally met you two, my dearest friends.

740080710.text: Huh... So that's what's going on.

740080711.text: In any case, I'm just relieved to hear that you never told anyone else about me. Phew! I just know I picked the right people to be my partners! Only your best friends can be relied on to keep your secrets.

740080712.text: Yep! Don't worry, Virgil, we won't tell anyone else about you.

740080713.text: ...Hahaha. I have complete confidence that you will never ever tell another soul about me.

740080714.text: Let's go! The treasure's waiting for us.

740080715.text: Yep yep! Here we come, treasure!

740081201.text: Waaah! That'd be terrible... All that delicious food, drowned and lost forever...

740081601.text: Though... All the places we've been have their own charm, too. It's not like Fontaine is just better than everywhere else, right?

740081602.text: My friend, surely you cannot be serious? How can there be any place in Teyvat that's better than Fontaine?

740081603.text: Ah, Paimon was just trying to say that other places are also really special, too! Virgil, have you ever set foot outside of Fontaine?

740081604.text: My dearest Paimon, you should know that there's an old saying in Fontaine: "All waters lead to Fontaine."

740081605.text: It's not the people of Fontaine who should go out and see the world, but all the world who should come and witness Fontaine's glory. Don't get it backwards.

740081607.text: Of course they do! Anyway, my friends, why don't we keep going? The treasure's still waiting for us deep inside these ruins!

740081501.text: Paimon, why don't you show him that trick of yours again...

740081503.text: Hahaha, how fascinating! In any case, though, I think everyone would agree that humans and machines are not the same.

subQuests.subQuestName: Defeat the Ruin Guard and find a way to open the door

740081702.text: #Hm? What's wrong, {NICKNAME}? Hurry up and go find the treasure.

740083001.text: Oh, we were there for the rising water level crisis, too...

740083002.text: Oh, then you two know what I'm talking about. It's unfortunate, but at least it all worked out in the end.

740083003.text: Yeah, just thinking about it still gives Paimon the shivers. People were adrift in the water, and if help had come any later...

740081801.text: Ugh... Paimon sure hopes this ruin thing isn't going to suddenly stand up...

740081802.text: It's just a Ruin Grader. We can handle it...

740081803.text: Paimon's not worried about you being strong enough. Paimon's just scared that you'll break the treasure in the middle of the fight!

740081804.text: We don't even know if there's a treasure here to break.

740081805.text: There has to be! There... is, right?

740081901.text: This machine... Why does it look kind of... familiar...?

740081904.text: Well, since this order brought all kinds of mechanisms from other nations to this place, this is probably something they hauled over from some distant ruin as well.

740081905.text: Wah! Paimon just had a really scary thought... Wh—What if the so-called "treasure" is just their research findings, and has nothing to do with piles of Mora at all...?

740081907.text: #Yeah, you're right, {NICKNAME}... but Paimon still wants Mora!

740081908.text: If we had hundreds of millions of Mora, we could build a pretty house and invite all our friends over, just eating great food and having fun day after day!

740082001.text: But now that you mention it, this Liliacruces Forum really did a lot of research, didn't they? We saw so many Kameras along the way...

740082002.text: They were probably used to record the results of their experiments, right? And there's also a notebook here too, let's see...

740082004.text: It's hard to make out a lot of the words... It says, "When... something goes out of control, break... something else, something something, so damage can be controlled..."

740082101.text: There's a glass wall here, and it seems like there's a bunch of water behind it...

740082102.text: Look, there are cracks in the glass.

740082103.text: Ack! That looks dangerous! If the glass suddenly breaks, who knows where we'll get swept off to...

740082104.text: Let's find the treasure quickly, and get the heck out of here!

subQuests.subQuestName: Try to break the glass barrier

740082202.text: Very well. But please allow me to remind you to make it quick. Treasure hates waiting.

740082402.text: Your wish is my command. Please, follow me. Our destination is not far from the Court of Fontaine...

740080101.text: #I must say, the weather today is simply wonderful! You are quite the {M#dashing young gentleman}{F#beautiful young lady}! Virgil, at your service.

740080103.text: Uh, um, a pleasure! Paimon's Paimon! And is at your service, too!

740080106.text: Ah, such elegant names! Welcome to the Court of Fontaine, it is truly an honor to meet the two of you here.

740080107.text: Ugh, Paimon can't stand much more of this...

740080108.text: How did you know we're not from Fontaine?

740080109.text: Hmph, with a glance, it is obvious that you're unciv—

740080111.text: ...That you're unsatisfied with being bathed in the soft lights of the city, but feel the call of the wild, which will never be illuminated by bright city lights! Yes, just like the heroes in the operas!

740080112.text: #Yeah, that's totally true! {NICKNAME} is an adventurer too, ad astra abyssosque and all that jazz!

740080113.text: Ha, I knew it. Those of the Adventurers' Guild are beggarly...

740080115.text: ...Courageous warriors begging with all their heart to unlock the deepest mysteries of the world! They wake with their eyes to the stars above, and sleep with their back to the abyss below! Where there is an unknown Domain, there is an adventurer who simply must explore it! Bravery bursting beyond the brim!

740080116.text: I could not help but notice how your gaze is focused on many things. Perhaps you wish to study our sublime arts, our intricate clockwork meka, or our advanced civic culture!

740080302.text: #Good heavens, {NICKNAME}, you certainly have a way with these Meka.

740080303.text: Phew! We must be getting close to the treasure. After all, we've already run into the guards!

740080304.text: Though Fontaine's achievements are as numerous and dazzling as the stars in the sky, the clockwork meka are undoubtedly the most exquisite of them all! Though, perhaps I shouldn't overpraise. One of the most exquisite.

740080305.text: You must have traveled via aquabus when you visited the Court, correct? Tell me you've seen the intricate Steambird as well. In Fontaine, even blacksmithing is done by Meka!

740080306.text: Why, the Maison Gardiennage didn't even have to lift a finger to beat me up. They just sent out some Gardemeks! It hurt so much, there was no choice but to submit...

740080308.text: I mean, beat up the bad guys! Why would they ever beat me up?

740080309.text: Whoa! If Meka are already so advanced, then surely the people of Fontaine don't need to do anything for themselves anymore, and can just leave everything to machines!

740080310.text: Hahaha, that's a good one, my dear friend, you're just adorable! It's a lot cheaper to hire a human than buy a clockwork meka. Or to put it another way, no one and nothing can infringe on a Fontaine citizen's right to work!

740080903.text: #Really? You think so? I seem to remember you handling it just fine back then, {NICKNAME}...

740081001.text: Well, knowing their extensive resources, it couldn't have been too hard for them to get their hands on these kinds of things. After all, this is the fabulously wealthy Liliacruces Forum we're talking about here!

740081002.text: Hmm, but we've also explored a lot of domains and seen more than our fair share of cool things during our adventures.

740081003.text: Is that so? Then I presume you've also found a lot of treasure?

740081006.text: How fascinating. I mean, what a terrific achievement. I expected nothing less from the two of you.

740081007.text: It's too bad that this place is completely flooded. It really feels like a lot happened here, and they made a lot of important discoveries...

740081008.text: The water levels of Fontaine have risen before. And according to the folks at the Fontaine Research Institute, they will rise again in the future. Perhaps one day, all of Fontaine will disappear beneath the waves.

740082502.text: Very well. But please allow me to remind you to make it quick. Treasure hates waiting.

740082701.text: Last time we saw them was in the deserts of Sumeru.

740082801.text: How will we open that door and proceed onward...

740082802.text: Ooh, so this is the "Forum" you were talking about! There are so many books everywhere — they must really have been dedicated to studying and conducting research...

740082803.text: Paimon would never have guessed that they were a secret society plotting to overthrow the government of Fontaine!

740082804.text: As the saying goes, dear Paimon, "Knowledge is power." This is especially true for the Liliacruces Forum.

740082805.text: You should understand that with great knowledge comes great power. And once great power is yours to command... There will only be one path left to you.

740082806.text: Uh... Paimon doesn't think that logic really holds water, but you're the local, not Paimon, so Paimon'll trust you know what you're talking about and leave it at that!

740082807.text: They seem to have been researching some amazing things, though. And we've already seen plenty of stuff that obviously isn't from here on the way...

740089901.text: Y'know, Paimon would love to see what you look like in diving gear!

740089902.text: Please take extra care in your investigation, you two.

740089903.text: The nearby water bodies may contain valuable resources and clues left behind by the Forum.

740089904.text: Please wait, you're going too fast! ... I suppose you aren't run-of-the-mill travelers after all...

740089905.text: Huh, Paimon didn't think there'd be an underwater ruin like this...

740089906.text: Behold, the ruins of the Liliacruces Forum!

740089907.text: Well, it's become a sanctuary for all kinds of aquatic life now.

740089909.text: To think that the key would be here...

740089910.text: Hmm? Have you been here before, Virgil?

740089911.text: Not long ago, my dear Paimon, my companions and I were stopped dead in front of the gate ahead, for we were not as quick-witted as the two of you.

740089912.text: Well, it's good that you met us then, isn't it?

740089913.text: Well said! It is my good fortune indeed!

740089914.text: Virgil, do we really have to continue looking for soaked pieces of paper?

740089915.text: Hmm? Oh, that. Well, no, not anymore— unless you're interested in that sort of thing, anyway.

740089916.text: Huh. Didn't you say that "things that are soaked rotten have their soaked rotten value" or something?

740089917.text: Yes... I suppose, dear friends, you could say something like, "the situation has changed."

740089918.text: Really...? Well, you're the local, so we'll take your word for it!

740089919.text: Whoa, hundreds of millions of Mora...

740089921.text: Gah, Paimon's pissed! We're gonna find that guy, and we're gonna settle the score!

740089922.text: Under the relentless assault of the raging waters, the Ruin Grader ceases to function.\nBut you and Paimon are swept away...

740089923.text: You arrive with Virgil at a place that seems a bit deserted.\nVirgil is wearing diving gear that looks difficult to move about in.
